speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Given the fact that around the world, there is a considerable degree of experimentation right now, even by developed countries in Europe and elsewhere to cultivate seaweed in coastal waters because of the benefits in terms of the emissions and also in terms of biodiversity and given that there is some experimentation around using technology to do this efficiently, would the Government be open to considering those kind of proposals in light of those benefits amid new developments and technologies.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We are aware that there have been efforts in different parts of the world to try and look at seaweed cultivation as a means of commercially providing substrates either for pharmaceutical use or for consumption.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But in looking at whether seaweed is suitable here, we have to  first depend on commercial assessments to see whether this is something that industry players think is viable.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Just for information, as I said in my main reply, we are looking at whether there is enough local consumption demand to generate that commercial interest.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And secondly, whether that really meets our nutritional goals.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: On the first point, broadly speaking, seaweed is not really a widely consumed item in Singapore as compared to the other food types like vegetables.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, in terms of the commercial viability and the local demand, it may well be a commercial calculation that there is really no big demand here.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The second thing is on experimentation of seaweed cultivation at the coastal area.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Here, we have also got to be very careful.
